categories.main_business_segments: Treasure Factory operates primarily in the reuse (secondhand retail) business, including general reuse shops, specialty stores for clothing, branded goods, sports/outdoor equipment, and furniture. The company also runs related businesses such as B2B auctions, moving services, rental services, real estate, and system development through its subsidiaries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company's core operational methods include multi-channel procurement of used goods (in-store, home visit, and delivery-based purchases), efficient inventory management via logistics centers, and the integration of physical stores with e-commerce platforms. IT and digital systems, including proprietary app and web development, support business efficiency and innovation.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Treasure Factory serves a broad consumer base seeking affordable secondhand goods, including individuals interested in clothing, home appliances, furniture, branded items, sports equipment, and hobby goods. The company also targets event-goers for rental services and customers needing moving or estate liquidation services.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in Japan, with a strong presence in the Kanto, Kansai, Chubu, and Kyushu regions. It has expanded internationally with subsidiaries and stores in Thailand and Taiwan, and plans further overseas expansion.
categories.supply_chain_position: Treasure Factory operates downstream in the supply chain as a retailer and service provider, sourcing goods directly from consumers and businesses, and selling to end-users through both physical and online channels.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include aggressive store expansion, investment in new and adjacent businesses, overseas growth, M&A for synergistic opportunities, and digital transformation (DX) leveraging IT and AI for operational efficiency and new business creation. The company also emphasizes sustainability and human capital development.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of secondhand goods in physical stores and online, as well as through rental fees, moving and real estate services, B2B auction commissions, and franchise royalties.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Treasure Factory competes with other major reuse shop chains and online C2C platforms in Japan's expanding secondhand market. The company differentiates itself through multi-format store operations, a strong physical and digital presence, and a comprehensive service offering.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2025, consolidated sales reached 42.2 billion yen, with operating profit at 4.0 billion yen and net profit attributable to shareholders at 2.7 billion yen, all showing over 20% year-on-year growth. The company operates 293 stores (including franchises) and employs over 1,200 people, with a robust growth trajectory and plans for 30–40 new stores annually.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Treasure Factory emphasizes a stable and diverse supply of quality secondhand goods, convenience through multi-channel purchasing and sales, and a seamless integration of physical and online experiences. Its broad service portfolio, sustainability focus, and ability to meet diverse lifestyle needs set it apart from competitors.
